h1:
What to Eat in Prachinburi
Dishes Worth the Stop
intro: Prachinburi is a town most people just drive through on the way to Khao Yai, but the food here has a character of its own. From rich-broth boat noodles that locals eat for breakfast, to the famous cotton-soft krathon fruit, the herbal dishes tied to Abhaibhubejhr, and simple meals by a waterfall, this is the food that makes Prachinburi worth a stop more than you'd expect.

blocks.html: When locals talk about food in Prachinburi, boat noodles come up first, followed by krathon fruit in season and the herbal cooking linked to Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital. The town doesn't have a lot of fancy restaurants, but the local food is honest and easy on the wallet. We've picked out the best dishes in town, seasonal souvenirs to take home, and meals with a nature backdrop.

blocks.text: Boat noodles, the town's signature bowl

blocks.html: Prachinburi is genuine boat-noodle country. Plenty of shops open early and sell them as a main meal, not a snack. The draw is the deeply simmered broth: some shops add herbs, others lean on tender braised pork or beef. Prices start very low, but people order several bowls per sitting, the way boat noodles are meant to be eaten.

items.name: Kuay Teow Ruea Nai Tin
items.blurb: One of the most talked-about shops among Prachinburi locals. The broth is rich enough to eat as-is without extra seasoning, and the braised pork and beef are meltingly tender. Beyond the noodles there's a braised-beef pad kaprao that many people order alongside, plus fresh crispy pork crackling for nibbling.
items.meta: Suwannason Rd, old Route 33, Dong Khilek subdistrict · Open 08:30–16:00

items.name: Kuay Teow Ruea Mesa Singha
items.blurb: A long-running boat-noodle shop in town. The signature is herbal braised beef in a fragrant, easy-to-eat broth. A solid pick for an early breakfast or lunch before heading off to explore.

items.name: Herbal-recipe noodle shop
items.blurb: A spot for herb-simmered broth and old-style braised pork, with a strong aroma of spices that anyone who likes bold flavors will appreciate. Open mornings to early afternoon only, so come before noon.

blocks.title: Insider tip
blocks.html: Many of Prachinburi's well-known boat-noodle shops sell out before mid-afternoon, and some close on odd days. Check the shop's page before you set out to be sure, and bring cash, since plenty of places still don't fully accept transfers.

Krathon (santol) has been tied to Prachinburi's name for a long time, especially the "pui fai" (cotton) variety grown around Si Maha Phot district. The flesh around the seeds is fluffy and white like cotton, with few seeds and large fruit, some weighing over a kilo, and a nicely balanced sweet-sour taste. The harvest peaks mid-year, roughly June to July, and if you come in season you'll see it for sale along the roads and all over the markets.

items: Fresh — peel off the thick skin and dip in chili-salt or sweet fish sauce; sour-sweet and refreshing, the most traditional way to eat it
Krathon loi kaew / krathon song khrueang — turned into desserts and boldly seasoned snacks, found at markets and souvenir shops in season
Bagged krathon — many orchards bag the fruit on the tree for smooth skin and tender flesh, the grade people buy as gifts rather than for themselves

blocks.title: Buying krathon worth your money
blocks.html: Krathon is at its best in June and July; out of season it's hard to find and pricey. Pick fruit with creamy-yellow skin that gives slightly when pressed, which is sweeter than the firm ones. If you're buying it as a gift, tell the vendor how many days you'll keep it so they can match the ripeness.

Prachinburi is home to Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Hospital, famous for Thai herbal medicine. That knowledge of herbs has worked its way into the local food too. Shops in this style turn flowers, leaves, and herbs into dishes you actually eat, not just plate garnishes, making them a good bet if you want to try something you won't find easily in other towns.

items.name: Ban Lao Rueang Mueang Samunphrai
items.blurb: A restaurant under the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Foundation, set in a classic old wooden house. Standout dishes include butterfly-pea glass-noodle salad, butterfly-pea rad na noodles, flower tempura, and "sun eggs," plus herbal drinks like butterfly-pea soda. It's the one place where you can both eat and learn about herbs at the same time.
items.meta: Next to the City Pillar Shrine · Open daily 10:00–20:00

blocks.html: Right nearby you can walk on to the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building and the herb garden, plus the Abhaibhubejhr herbal-products shop where you can grab souvenirs to take home, from inhalers and herbal compress balls to herbal soap. You can eat and shop your way through one neighborhood.

Prachinburi borders the lower Isan region, so a good share of locals eat som tam, grilled chicken, larb, and nam tok as everyday meals. Bold-flavored Isan shops are easy to find across town and in the outer districts, prices are wallet-friendly, and they make a relaxed dinner.

items.name: Isan shop in the Si Maha Phot area
items.blurb: Som tam, grilled chicken, and grilled pork neck with true bold Isan flavors at easy prices, handy for a stop on the way to the krathon orchards or Emerald Pool.

items.name: Made-to-order shop in town
items.blurb: Pad kaprao, spicy stir-fries, tom yum, easy meals that Prachinburi locals really eat every day, found around the market and community areas.

blocks.text: Meals by the waterfall and in nature

blocks.html: One of Prachinburi's charms is eating by the water. Khao Ito Waterfall in Khao Ito Forest Park, Ban Phra subdistrict, has shallow pools to soak your feet in and food stalls right by the falls. The menu is simple stuff like som tam, grilled chicken, sticky rice, and fried snacks. You eat with your feet in the cool water, an atmosphere the in-town shops just can't offer.

items: Khao Ito Waterfall — closest to town, with food stalls and waterside seating, open around 09:00–16:00, ideal for a weekend lunch
Khao Yai zone on the Prachinburi side — heading up toward Kabin Buri and Prachantakham districts you'll find more and more cafes and mountain-view spots, great for a coffee in the cool breeze
Roadside snacks on the Khao Yai route — boiled corn, fried bananas, and seasonal fruit sold along the road as you drive up the hill, easy to grab on the way

blocks.title: Planning a waterfall meal
blocks.html: The waterfall has the most water and the best atmosphere in the rainy season (roughly June–October); in the dry season the flow can be low. Arrive before noon to grab a good waterside seat, and bring cash, since most stalls by the falls only take cash.

blocks.text: A one-day eat-and-explore Prachinburi, no rush

blocks.html: With just one day you can easily fit in boat noodles, herbal dishes, and a waterfall meal. Here's a rough guide where nothing is too far apart.

items.activity: Start the morning with boat noodles
items.note: Hit a popular shop before they sell out, and order several bowls boat-noodle style

items.activity: Stop by the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building and herb garden
items.note: Walk the old building and pick up herbal souvenirs

items.activity: Lunch at Ban Lao Rueang Mueang Samunphrai
items.note: Try the butterfly-pea glass-noodle salad and flower tempura
Soak your feet, play in the water, and order som tam and grilled chicken by the water

faq.q: What's the must-try food in Prachinburi?
faq.a: First up is the rich-broth boat noodles that are the town's signature dish, followed by seasonal cotton-soft krathon, Abhaibhubejhr-style herbal dishes like butterfly-pea glass-noodle salad, and a meal by Khao Ito Waterfall with som tam and grilled chicken.

faq.q: Where should I eat boat noodles in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Shops people mention often include Kuay Teow Ruea Nai Tin in Dong Khilek subdistrict and Mesa Singha in town. Most open from morning to early afternoon and sell out fast, so come before noon and bring cash.

faq.q: When is krathon in season in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Prachinburi's cotton-soft krathon peaks mid-year, roughly June to July. That's when you'll see it for sale most along the roads and at markets. Out of season it's hard to find and prices climb.

faq.q: Where can I eat Abhaibhubejhr herbal food?
faq.a: Ban Lao Rueang Mueang Samunphrai, under the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr Foundation, is open daily 10:00–20:00 next to the City Pillar Shrine. You can walk on to the Chao Phraya Abhaibhubejhr building and herb garden in the same area.

faq.q: Are there waterside restaurants by the falls in Prachinburi?
faq.a: Yes. Khao Ito Waterfall in Khao Ito Forest Park, Ban Phra subdistrict, has stalls selling som tam, grilled chicken, and fried snacks right by the falls where you can soak your feet. It's best in the rainy season when the water is high.
